# useViewTransition

Runs a navigation as a same-document view transition, for a router adapter to call. It uses the browser's `document.startViewTransition` where there is one and motion is not reduced, under `<OuroProvider motion="reduced">` or the device's setting, and swaps the view at once everywhere else. A transition moves no focus and changes no title: the swap does both, as it does without one, so the focus and the announced title are the same either way.

```tsx
import { useViewTransition } from "@/registry/ouro/lib/ouro/use-view-transition";
```

## Example

```tsx
// React Router. app/components/ouro-router-link.tsx:
import type { ComponentProps } from "react";
import { Link } from "react-router";
import type { OuroLinkComponent } from "@/lib/ouro/use-ouro";
import { useViewTransition } from "@/lib/ouro/use-view-transition";

export function OuroRouterLink({ href, ...props }: ComponentProps<OuroLinkComponent>) {
  const { enabled } = useViewTransition();
  return <Link to={href} viewTransition={enabled} {...props} />;
}

// Any router, from code:
const { run } = useViewTransition();
await run(() => navigate("/recipes/42"));
```

## Usage

Only the element that moves between views (the opened row's avatar or title) takes a `view-transition-name`, since a name repeated across rows makes the browser skip the transition. Keep a transition short, because a press during one lands on its overlay.

Ouro UI takes no router, so you give `run` the swap: a state update, which `run` flushes inside the transition, or a router's `navigate` whose promise settles once the new view has rendered. Where a router has its own `viewTransition` prop, pass it `enabled`. The browser runs the back and forward buttons' swap itself, so only navigations you start go through `run`. Import it only where a navigation needs it.

Use it instead of calling `document.startViewTransition` yourself, which ignores `<OuroProvider motion>` and the device's reduced-motion setting.

## Returns

`ViewTransitionControls`

## Types

### `ViewSwap`

What a navigation does to the page: it may return a promise that settles once the new view is in the document.

```ts
type ViewSwap = () => void | Promise<void>;
```

### `ViewTransitionControls`

What `useViewTransition` returns.

```ts
interface ViewTransitionControls {
  /** Whether a navigation may animate: `false` under reduced motion, from the device or `<OuroProvider motion="reduced">`. Pass it to a router's own `viewTransition` prop. */
  enabled: boolean;
  /** Runs `swap` inside a view transition where the browser has them and motion is not reduced; otherwise runs it at once. Resolves when the new view is in the document, not when the animation ends. */
  run: (swap: ViewSwap) => Promise<void>;
}
```
